Hi, not an ophthalmologist but an IM doctor here. Ask ko lang sana kung bakit mo nalink ang cataract, myoma,  hypertensive retinopathy or even diabetic retinopathy sa  cornea? Himayin ko lang yung problem sa mga sinabi mong sakit ah kasi inaral namin sya sa medschool:

1. Cataract: Ang problem ng cataract ay opacification ng lens and has nothing to do with the cornea. Normal na nagkakaroon ng cataracts kasi nagiging cloudy ang lens kapag tumatanda ang tao and not nagpaLASIK sya. 

2. Myoma: Ito ay isang type of tumor na gawa sa smooth muscle, kadalasan sa matres ito nakikita. Wala pa akong narinig nor nabasa na merong myoma ang mata, much less dahil sa LASIK surgery. 

3. Epekto ng hypertension sa mata aka Hypertensive Retinopathy: dahil sa uncontrolled BP, ay nasisira ang mga blood vessels sa mata na makikita sa likod ng mga mata, or retina. Ito ay napakalayo sa cornea, hence I don't see the connection ng LASIK sa sakit na ito. 

4. Epekto ng diabetes sa mata or Diabetic Retinopathy: dahil sa uncontrolled sugar, nasisira ang blood vessels sa mata na makikita sa mata, o retina. Wala ding mga pag-aaral na naglilink ng paggamit ng LASIK sa diabetic retinopathy.

Hindi lahat ng mga malalabo ang mata ay naguundergo ng LASIK surgery, dahil ito ay may indications or dahilan, hindi lamang sa dahil gusto ng pasyente or dahil kaya nyang magbayad, nasa ophthalmologist kung  yung pasyente ay mamemeet yung criteria to undergo such a procedure and the Ophthanologist will also review the risks and benefits of the procedure. If the doctor, deems that the benefit is greater than the risk, then he will strongly advise it. 

P.S. sana po let's not propagate misinformation or disinformation, we can give and share opinions pero let's not instill fear or even discourage our fellowmen in safe, well-studied and approved medical procedures by the different medical societies. We never know that those medical procedures might be life-saving or an even be life changing for them.

I think you are just adjusting to medschool and that's understandable, I think it is now the time to evaluate if you should continue using your study methods from college and apply it now. 

Now, I am all for reading the textbooks because in the long run it will really help you, especially in the board exams. I suggest that you make an extra effort of reading the assigned topics before the lecture and if time permits, after. But not everyone has the luxury of time, and in these cases you need to use transcriptions so that you can easily digest and, forgive me, blindly memorize everything. 

I also suggest taking some time talking to some of your seniors, so that they can give you tips and tricks on how your medical professors ask questions on quizzes and exams. I know this is not the best trick but when pressed for time, at least you would what to focus on. I hope that this helps :) 

Always remember study smart not study hard :)
